title: Emergency delivery and third stage
stem: ED delivery room. A woman at 39 weeks in her second pregnancy is pushing, with the head crowning. The obstetric team is 15 minutes away. Conduct the delivery and the third stage on the manikin.
notes:
Checked against NICE NG235 (Intrapartum care, 2023) and RCOG guidance.

Prepare two teams (mother, baby), PPE, warm towels. Controlled delivery of the head: flex it with the palm and guard the perineum; ask her to pant rather than push as the head crowns. Feel for a nuchal cord (slip it over the head if loose; 'somersault' delivery if tight — clamping and cutting before delivery is a last resort). Wait for restitution; deliver the anterior shoulder with gentle downward traction with the next contraction, then the posterior shoulder upwards. Baby dried and placed skin to skin; delayed cord clamping for at least 60 seconds in a well baby (NICE). Routine suctioning is not recommended.

Third stage (NICE): active management — oxytocin 10 IU IM after the birth of the anterior shoulder or after the baby, deferred cord clamping, then controlled cord traction after signs of separation (gush of blood, cord lengthening, fundus rises and becomes globular), guarding the uterus above the pubis to avoid inversion. Check the placenta and membranes are complete, check for tears, and estimate blood loss. Prolonged third stage (NICE NG235): not completed within 30 minutes with active management, or 60 minutes with physiological management. Your notes' 30 minutes is correct for active management.

Your notes choose Syntometrine for routine use; NICE recommends oxytocin 10 IU IM (fewer side effects: vomiting, hypertension). Syntometrine is contraindicated in pre-eclampsia, as your notes say.

steps.label: Third stage
steps.hint: Oxytocin IM, wait for separation signs, controlled cord traction guarding the uterus, check placenta and tears.

opts.t: Wait for signs of separation: gush of blood, cord lengthens, uterus firms and rises
Controlled cord traction with the other hand guarding the uterus above the pubis

opts.t: Check placenta and membranes complete; three vessels in the cord
opts.mark: Checks placenta, membranes and cord vessels

opts.t: Check the fundus is contracted; inspect for tears; estimate blood loss
opts.mark: Checks tone, tears and blood loss

opts.t: Pull hard on the cord straight away
opts.r: Traction before separation, without guarding the uterus, risks uterine inversion.
